brief: Quest engine and journal. Spec was orchestration/status/W1-19-r3.json: the quest machine is barely driven by play — 6 verbs with no caller outside harness/api.js, note() covering 11 of 120 quests, takeBranch() zero callers, and 113 of 121 (quest,reveal) pairs a resolution demands with no route in play across 8 unread channels.
headline: THE MODEL WITH NO READER WAS `deceit.revealed_by` ITSELF — 186 authored rows naming, for every truth a resolution demands, exactly who or what tells you, and `channel`/`source` had ZERO readers in game/src/. Built the reader for the two channels whose sources exist as people: 48 of 121 demanded reveals now have a route in play, was 8. Talking to the person the quest file names now gives you what they know AND writes the journal entry that IS that truth — note()'s world-side coverage goes from 11 quests to 48. Proved in a browser end to end on Q-MAIN-01 with two controls, and delete-the-fix takes 37/37 machine legs to 0/37.
next_step: hand to a critic. NOT DONE and not faked: 73 demanded reveals still have no route. The mainline is still blocked at Q-MAIN-06 and the viability walk will still report 0/40 — its two reveals are `ledger`, and `item_the_drowned_tally` is not an object anywhere in this build. See `left unrouted, and why` below; the next piece is a readable-document object, not another reader.
notes: THE FINDING, RESTATED AS A CENSUS I TOOK RATHER THAN INHERITED. The 9 channels split by whether `source` names something that EXISTS in this build, and the split is not close. PEOPLE: talk_to_target 18 of 28 demanded sources are rows in game/data/npcs/**, rival_npc 22 of 23, eavesdrop 7 of 9, corpse 1 of 1. OBJECTS: ledger 1 of 28, letter 0 of 6, environment 0 of 18 — their sources are `item_*`/`loc_*` ids and, for nine of them, sentences ('the cough on the lichen beds'). 22 `item_` ids exist in the whole tree; the ledger channel alone names 34 that do not.

So the people channels were never blocked on content. They were blocked on a READER: `deceit.revealed_by[].channel` and `.source` — 186 rows — were read by NOTHING in game/src/. `Engine._bookKnowledgeIndex()` reads `.source` for `channel: 'book'` and that was the whole of it. Building the reader is the fix; authoring 51 more hooks.json rows would have been a second model to keep in sync with the first.

The schema says the same thing in its own words: quest.schema.json's gloss on `requires_knowing` is 'the mechanism by which TALKING TO THE TARGET before killing them opens a door'. That door had no handle.

BUILT (1/3) — game/src/sim/quest/reveal-routes.js. `buildRevealRoutes(defs)` indexes `"person:<npcId>" -> rows`. Pure over the quest definitions, so the audit builds the same index with no engine. Rows sort by the JOURNAL INDEX they write, not by reveal id: one person can be the source of two reveals of the same quest (Ee-Vashum tells you both of Q-XULA-03's, entries 46 and 54) and the journal is append-only and monotonic — sorted by id those land 54 before 46 and journal.js THROWS. That was a real crash in a world action, found by running it.

BUILT (2/3) — QuestEngine.learnFrom(kind, source). Offers every row the index has for that pair and REFUSES OR TAKES each one with a stated reason, returning the refusals as well as the grants. Three conditions and none is decoration: (a) the quest must be OPEN, because `reveal()` alone mints a row (foreknowledge) and without this line 30 of the 40 routed rows fire on a character with an empty journal — every person in the province spilling the middle of jobs you have not taken; (b) `before_point_of_no_return: false` waits for the crossing, which is what the schema's own gloss on that field means; (c) a declared `journal` index is written through `note()`, pre-checked for existence, terminal state and backwards writes so a world action never throws.

BUILT (3/3) — the call site, Engine.talkTo(), beside the `opens_by.overheard_from` block that already lives there. Same doctrine as its neighbour: walking up to the person who knows is how you come to know. `talkTo` throws unless `sim.findNPC` returns somebody, so the route inherits the presence term honestly — a reveal whose source is nowhere stays unlearnable and the audit counts it UNROUTED.

THE JOURNAL HALF, which is the other half of this item's brief. `note()` — the verb that writes the MIDDLE of a journal — had one caller in game/src/, the hooks.json journal branch, covering 11 of 120 quests. AM-QST04-W1-18-02 adds an OPTIONAL `deceit.revealed_by[].journal`: the entry that IS this truth in prose. Authored, never inferred — 37 indices hand-picked against the prose. In most cases the entry was already written and unreachable, which is the whole shape of this defect: Q-MAIN-06's journal 40 IS rev_the_curve_predates and 55 IS rev_the_steward_named.

NUMBERS, at 7d9a8e1, `node tools/quests/reveal-route-audit.mjs`. Section A: demanded reveals with a route in play 8 -> 48 of 121. talk_to_target 0/28 -> 18/28, rival_npc 0/23 -> 22/23. Quests with EVERY resolution blocked 8 -> 7; Q-MAIN-26, Act V's pressable pre-violence conversation with the antagonist, is off that list. Section D (new): 37 legs run, 37 pass, 37 journal entries written by note() from play.

DELETE-THE-FIX 1 (the router), `--falsify no-router`: empty `revealRoutes` and the SAME 37 legs go 37/37 -> 0/37 with 0 journal entries written. The two arms genuinely differ; the reveals are not arriving from somewhere else.

DELETE-THE-FIX 2 (the call site): removed the `learnFrom` line from Engine.talkTo() on a copy and the audit's call-site assertion goes true -> false and the tool exits 1. This is the check that stops the exact failure the last round found — a correct model wired to nothing.

DELETE-THE-FIX 3 (the schema amendment): removed `journal` from quest.schema.json and quest-audit --schema goes 53/120 -> 31/120 validating, 22 quests newly failing on `additionalProperties`. The amendment is load-bearing, not decorative.

NON-VACUITY, which is where the last round's first attempt died. Section D only RUNS a leg if the resolution gate refused BY NAME before the act; a leg that ran and learned nothing is a FAILURE, not a skip; and the `--falsify` arm INVERTS the verdict so a run where legs still pass is the failure. The first version of the section passed Q-MAIN-32 by refusing everything, and Q-MAIN-32's reveal is `before_point_of_no_return: false` — so the leg now PLAYS Q-MAIN-27/res_cross through `_applyConsequences` to stand in the world where that row is reachable, rather than being scored red for a refusal that is correct.

PROVED IN THE RUNNING GAME, one browser, `node tools/quests/reveal-route-world.mjs`, report at reports/runs/W1-18-R2/reveal-route-world.json. Q-MAIN-01: walk to Gideon, talk to `gideon-court-factor`. knows [] -> [rev_factor]. journal [10] -> [10, 45] — the MIDDLE of the journal, written because a player talked to somebody. CONTROL 1, the wrong person (antiquarian-decius-arral): learned nothing. CONTROL 2, the right person before the job is taken: learned nothing. `questReveal`, `questNote` and `questSetFlag` are never called and the tool asserts against its own bytes that it does not name them; `__ENGINE`, the documented back door, likewise.

DECLARED GRANTS in that browser run, and they are the honest cost of it: `questOpen` and `learnTopic` (only the `opens_by` topic the refusal named — 'the drowned tally'). Whether THIS character could have been OFFERED the quest is the offer gate's question and belongs to mainline-findability.mjs. `learnTopic` writes `topicsKnown` — what you can ASK ABOUT — which is a different register from `know:`, and `know:` has one writer and that writer is what is under test. `populateSettlement`/`populateSite` walk into the town each person's OWN RECORD names; nobody is spawned from nothing.

ONLY ONE CASE RAN IN THE BROWSER, said plainly. All 36 candidates refuse at a cold start and 34 of them refuse on a faction ladder or a prerequisite quest, which no honest grant clears. One case is enough to prove the WIRING — that `talkTo` reaches `learnFrom` in the real Engine — and the breadth is section D's 37. A critic who wants more browser breadth needs a character that has climbed a ladder, which is W1-FACTIONS' fixture, not mine.

LEFT UNROUTED, AND WHY. ledger (28 demanded), letter (6) and environment (18) — 52 of the remaining 73 — are blocked on CONTENT, not on a reader. `item_the_drowned_tally` is not an object anywhere in this build and neither are the other 33 ledgers, the 6 letters or `loc_the_flooding_road`; nine environment sources are not ids at all. Wiring a reader to those produces a table of routes to nothing, which is the failure this round exists to stop. What they need is a readable-document object and a place to find it — and then `_bookKnowledgeIndex` already shows the shape.

LEFT UNROUTED (2). eavesdrop (9 demanded) is NOT routed even though 7 of its 9 sources are real people, because the only conversation action this build has is `talkTo`, which is walking up and being greeted — the opposite of eavesdropping. Routing it there would give a player who introduced themselves credit for having listened unobserved, and would quietly make the stealth system decorative for the one thing it is most obviously for. It needs a proximity-and-not-noticed reader against sim/stealth.

LEFT UNROUTED (3). corpse (1 demanded, Q-MAIN-11 / npc-sexton-ivo-sarn). `discoverCorpse()` is the CRIME system's event for a WITNESS finding a body, not the player examining one, and there is no search-a-body action in game/src/ to hang it on. One row; not worth inventing an action for.

REPORTED, NOT FIXED (a). 15 person-channel rows name somebody who is not in game/data/npcs/** at all — clerk-meno, npc-ossei, npc-eleen, cutter-ashaan-hulei, npc-ineel-sa, npc-skara-hull-chalk, npc-ineve-corrano, npc-widow-tesla-vor, npc-ishi-vaal, npc-sorel-ithan, npc-river-band-elder, npc-uneel-vaakh-sister, npc-high-hollow-speaker, npc-fourth-day-boatman, npc-sexton-ivo-sarn. The audit counts them UNROUTED and lists them rather than scoring a route to nobody green. They are a cast list, and writing them is cheap.

REPORTED, NOT FIXED (b). `takeBranch()` still has zero callers anywhere, and it is not cosmetic: `branches[].leads_to` may name a `deceit.revealed_by` entry and two mainline quests use that — Q-MAIN-01's `br_the_coat` leads to `rev_factor`, Q-MAIN-02's `br_ninety` leads to `rev_ojal`. So the file says those reveals arrive by taking a fork, and this round routes them by the person instead. Both are true of the fiction; the fork is the one with no world action, and a branch is a DECISION, which needs a place for the player to make it. Not invented here.

REPORTED, NOT FIXED (c). Q-ASSZ-06's `rev_corvo_hand` gets no `journal` index because the only entry that carries it is 10, which `open()` has already written — the quest opens with the truth in it. Q-MAIN-26's `rev_he_never_wrote_the_recension` gets none because its only entry is 92, a `success`, which `note()` correctly refuses. Both left unauthored rather than pointed somewhere plausible.

NEW CONTENT CHECK, armed only after the data existed (RULES.md rule 13). tools/check-quests.mjs now fails the COMMIT on a `revealed_by.journal` that names an entry the quest does not have or a terminal one. Four new self-test cases, two red and two green; `--self-test` is 10/10 and the live check is silent on the shipped tree.

GATES at 7d9a8e1: boot-check PASS, check-data PASS, check-quests PASS (+ self-test 10/10), check-content PASS, check-prose exit 0, corpus-index exit 0, quest-audit integrity problems 0. Schema validation 53/120 — unchanged by this round; the 40 failures are pre-existing (magic-utility's non-enum channels, missing `rewards`, non-enum `method`) and none of them mentions `journal`.

NO NEW SAVE FIELDS. `know:` flags have always lived in `q.quests[id].flags` and journal entries in `q.journal`; both are already carried by game/src/save/state.js. Nothing new to round-trip, so rule 7 has nothing new to catch here.

LOAD, per rule 26. Analysis and authoring were done entirely browserless while the box sat at 24-30 headless_shell and loadavg 17-24, which is over rule 21's cap. The single browser run was taken at 18 headless_shell / loadavg 11.9-16.1. NO TIMING FIGURE IS QUOTED ANYWHERE in this piece — every number is a count or a boolean, and neither moves with load.
